headline.headline: METS RALLY FROM THREE DOWN, THEN HOLD ON BY A THREAD IN 10-9 CLASSIC
headline.deck: New York scores five in the ninth, survives Atlanta's furious answer to steal road win
headline.body:
ATLANTA — The New York Mets arrived at Truist Park on Sunday as a fifth-place team 16 games under .500, facing a Braves club that owned first place in the National League East. What followed was the kind of game that makes no logical sense and perfect baseball sense at the same time. The Mets trailed 9-5 heading into the ninth inning, scratched out five runs against an Atlanta bullpen that had held New York scoreless through the fifth, sixth, seventh and eighth, and then watched with white-knuckled anxiety as Atlanta answered with six of its own — only to fall one run short at 10-9, final.

The Braves had drawn first blood with a three-run first inning before the Mets turned the game around in the second, plating four runs to seize a 5-3 advantage they would carry until Atlanta's bats came alive late. Winning pitcher D. Williams earned the decision in a game that stretched three hours and three minutes, including a one-hour, 47-minute delay. D. Baldwin was hit by a pitch from McLean during the contest, adding to a physical, chippy atmosphere before 28,621 fans at Truist Park.

The victory nudges the Mets to 38-53 while Atlanta drops to 52-37 in a series the Braves still lead, 2-1. For New York, a road win against the division leader — any road win, in any fashion — counts the same in the standings. The Mets will take it.

secondary.headline: TWINS THROTTLE YANKEES, 6-1, IN BRONX BLOWOUT
secondary.deck: Minnesota's Weathers dominates as New York's lineup goes quietly at home
secondary.body:
NEW YORK — The Minnesota Twins walked into Yankee Stadium on Sunday and walked out with a convincing 6-1 victory, as pitcher Weathers threw effectively and the Twins offense spread the damage across six of nine innings before 39,155 fans in the Bronx. Minnesota scored in the first, added another run in the fourth, broke the game open with two in the fifth and two more in the sixth to build an insurmountable cushion against a Yankees club that managed only a single run in the ninth inning.

Doubles from Martin, Lewis, Caratini, Lee and Grisham fueled Minnesota's attack. Weathers earned the win and also hit Keaschall by pitch in the contest, which finished in three hours and one minute. The Yankees, playing at home, left too many runners on base and never threatened seriously against Minnesota's pitching staff. The Twins left the Bronx with a statement win against one of the American League's marquee franchises.

secondary.headline: ROBINSON ADDRESSES PLAYOFF HAND INJURY, REVEALS FAMILY INCIDENT BEHIND IT
secondary.deck: New Celtics center says personal matter off the court triggered the injury that clouded his postseason
secondary.body:
BOSTON — Mitchell Robinson, who joined the Boston Celtics after his time with the New York Knicks and became a talking point throughout the NBA playoffs, addressed publicly Sunday the hand injury that raised questions about his availability during the postseason. Robinson confirmed the injury was a reaction to a family incident that occurred off the court, putting to rest speculation that the ailment was basketball-related.

The revelation adds a human dimension to a story that had swirled around the Celtics as they push through the conference semifinals. Robinson declined to elaborate on the specifics of the family situation, but the statement closes a chapter of uncertainty around Boston's frontcourt depth. The Celtics are among the teams still alive in a second round that has produced drama at every turn, and Robinson's health will remain a subject of close watch as the bracket narrows.

secondary.headline: MAHOMES, GOMEZ AMONG STARS AT KELCE-SWIFT WEDDING FESTIVITIES
secondary.deck: Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift celebrate at Madison Square Garden with an A-list guest list
secondary.body:
NEW YORK — Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes and pop star Selena Gomez were among the celebrities who descended on Madison Square Garden over the weekend for the wedding festivities of Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift, a union that has commanded tabloid and sports-page attention in equal measure since the couple went public. The venue choice — one of the most famous arenas in the world, in the middle of Manhattan — matched the scale of the occasion.

Kelce, the future Hall of Fame tight end who helped the Chiefs capture multiple Super Bowl championships before retiring, and Swift brought together two of the most recognizable brands in American entertainment. Mahomes, Kelce's longtime teammate and closest friend in football, was a centerpiece of the celebration. The wedding falls during the NFL offseason, giving the football world a moment to mark the end of one of the sport's great romances-turned-marriage without the distraction of the regular season.

column.headline: THE METS REMINDED US WHY BASEBALL NEVER GIVES UP ON ITSELF
column.body:
There is a temptation, when watching a 37-53 team play a 52-36 team, to stop paying attention somewhere around the seventh inning. Sunday in Atlanta was a reminder of why that temptation should always be resisted. The Mets trailed by four runs with three outs left, looked like precisely the kind of hopeless club their record advertises, and then erupted for five runs against a Braves bullpen that had been untouchable for seven innings straight. Then Atlanta came back with six of its own in the bottom of the ninth to nearly steal the win back. One run. That is what separated the outcome from a complete reversal of fortune.

The cynics will say the Mets are still 16 games under .500 and the Braves still lead the NL East by a comfortable margin, and the cynics will be correct. But baseball rewards the people who refuse to look away, and Sunday at Truist Park was the argument for staying until the last out in its purest form. In a summer when the NBA playoffs and NHL second round are producing their own drama, this game stood alone as the kind of absurd, grinding spectacle that only a 162-game season can generate. Do not let anyone tell you otherwise.

story.headline: METS STUN BRAVES WITH FIVE-RUN NINTH, THEN SURVIVE ATLANTA'S SIX-RUN ANSWER IN 10-9 THRILLER
story.deck: New York rallies from three down, holds on as Atlanta falls one run short in wild finale
story.body:
ATLANTA — The New York Mets trailed the Atlanta Braves by three runs heading into the ninth inning Sunday afternoon at Truist Park, scratched out five runs to take a lead, then watched in horror as Atlanta answered with six of its own — and somehow escaped with a 10-9 victory that left 28,621 fans stunned and a game clock reading three hours and three minutes, not counting a one-hour, 47-minute delay. Winning pitcher Williams D. earned the decision in the most chaotic ninth inning of the young summer, as the Braves pulled within one but could not push across the tying run.

The Mets had done their early damage in the second inning, plating four runs to wipe out a 3-1 Atlanta advantage built in the first. The game then went quiet for seven straight scoreless innings before the ninth-inning fireworks erupted. Homers by Taylor, his fifth of the year, and Ewing, also his fifth, provided the thrust of New York's five-run burst. Baldwin's 15th home run of the season headlined Atlanta's stunning six-run response, and Baldwin was also hit by a pitch from McLean during the frame. Doubles by Bichette, Baty, Albies, and Olson decorated the box score, while the Braves stranded 17 runners, a figure that haunted Atlanta's dugout long after the final out.

The loss stings for the Braves, who entered the day at 52-36 and leading the NL East, while the Mets sit at 37-53, fifth in the division. The series continues Monday, with Atlanta holding a 2-1 edge. Elsewhere Sunday, the Minnesota Twins roughed up the New York Yankees 6-1 at Yankee Stadium, with starter Weathers picking up the win before a crowd of 39,155 and piling up doubles from Martin, Lewis, Caratini, Lee, and Grisham as Minnesota left 27 runners on base. The Pittsburgh Pirates rolled past the Washington Nationals 11-5, powered by home runs from Lowe, his 21st, Reynolds, his 13th, Jr., his 19th, and Crews, his sixth, with Chandler earning the win.

story.headline: PETERSON ERUPTS FOR 28, BOOZER IMPRESSES AS ROOKIES MAKE SUMMER LEAGUE STATEMENTS
story.deck: Two highly touted first-round picks announce their arrivals with commanding debut performances.
story.body:
LAS VEGAS — Darryn Peterson and Cameron Boozer wasted no time making their professional intentions clear Sunday, delivering the kind of summer league debuts that have scouts buzzing and front offices nodding with satisfaction. Peterson, the electric guard who turned heads throughout the pre-draft process, torched defenders for 28 points in a performance that showcased his full offensive arsenal — pull-up jumpers, slashing drives and a composure that looked nothing like a player logging his first NBA-affiliated minutes. Boozer, son of former All-Star Carlos Boozer, complemented him with 15 points and a physicality in the paint that drew immediate comparisons to his father's early years.

Milwaukee's summer league roster also provided its own highlight when Duke Brennan threw down a thunderous slam that stopped the Vegas crowd cold and immediately circulated across social media. Brennan, fighting for a roster spot with the Bucks, used the dunk as an exclamation point on a performance that could strengthen his case heading into training camp.

Meanwhile, away from the desert heat, two significant front-office developments reshaped the league's landscape. New Celtic Mitchell Robinson broke his silence on the mysterious hand injury that shadowed the Knicks' NBA Finals run, revealing the wound stemmed from a family incident rather than a basketball-related cause. And in Washington, Georgetown and Knicks legend Patrick Ewing agreed to join head coach Brian Keefe's staff as an assistant with the rebuilding Wizards, bringing Hall of Fame credibility to a franchise hungry for a new identity.

story.headline: MINTYUKOV LOCKS UP WITH DUCKS AS ROBERTSON EYES ARBITRATION IN BUSY NHL OFFSEASON
story.deck: Anaheim secures its blue-line cornerstone while Dallas braces for a salary fight with its top scorer.
story.body:
The Anaheim Ducks moved swiftly Monday to secure the future of their defensive corps, re-signing restricted free agent Pavel Mintyukov to a five-year contract. The 22-year-old blueliner has emerged as one of the most promising young defensemen in the Western Conference, posting 17 goals and 52 assists over 204 games across his first three NHL seasons. The deal keeps Mintyukov off the open market and signals Anaheim's belief that its long rebuild is nearing a meaningful turning point.

In Dallas, the mood was less celebratory. Stars winger Jason Robertson filed for salary arbitration Monday, triggering a formal process that could force the two sides into a hearing this summer. Robertson, Dallas' leading scorer and one of the premier pure goal-scorers in the league, had previously declined a long-term offer from the Seattle Kraken in a potential sign-and-trade scenario. The filing puts the Stars in the uncomfortable position of either hammering out a deal before a hearing date or arguing Robertson's value before an arbitrator.

Elsewhere around the league, Nashville inked center Mavrik Bourque to a six-year, $33 million deal just three days after acquiring the 24-year-old, signaling confidence in his fit with the Predators' rebuild. Detroit added depth forward Chase Stillman on a one-year contract, bringing in the 23-year-old St. Louis native and former first-round pick of New Jersey to compete for a roster spot. The flurry of moves underscored just how active the 2026 NHL offseason has become since free agency opened June 30.

story.headline: QUARTERBACK CAROUSEL SPINS WILDLY AS TEAMS RESHAPE ROSTERS FOR 2026
story.deck: Three franchises swap signal-callers in a frantic May reshuffling of NFL depth charts.
story.body:
The NFL offseason turned frantic this week as the Las Vegas Raiders, Cleveland Browns, and Carolina Panthers all executed quarterback moves that will reshape their franchises heading into training camp. The Raiders agreed to terms with veteran Sam Darnold on a two-year, $58 million contract, giving first-year head coach Mike Vrabel a proven starter after a dismal 2025 campaign that produced only five wins. Cleveland, meanwhile, shipped struggling starter Deshaun Watson and the remainder of his guaranteed contract to a restructured deal that sends him to Carolina, where the Panthers are gambling that a change of scenery can resurrect a career that has cost the franchise more than $230 million in guaranteed money.

The draft class of 2026 continued to filter into team facilities as rookies reported for offseason programs across the league. Colorado quarterback Shedeur Sanders, selected fourth overall by the New York Giants, drew immediate attention at the team's East Rutherford facility, throwing alongside veteran backup Daniel Jones in what Giants offensive coordinator Mike Kafka called a legitimate open competition. Sanders completed 78 percent of his throws during the team's first organized team activity session Tuesday, impressing teammates with both his arm and his command of the playbook only weeks after hearing his name called in Green Bay.

On the trade front, the San Francisco 49ers sent disgruntled wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk to the Pittsburgh Steelers in exchange for a 2027 first-round pick and a second-round selection, ending a months-long standoff between the Pro Bowl receiver and San Francisco management. Aiyuk, who skipped voluntary workouts and requested a trade in March, will now line up alongside fellow wideout George Pickens in Pittsburgh, giving new Steelers offensive coordinator Ken Dorsey a pair of explosive perimeter threats to build around. The 49ers, for their part, plan to redirect the cap space toward shoring up an offensive line battered by injuries throughout the 2025 season.
